search_strategy: Read the code first (base_online_request_processor.py, the three provider processors, status tracker, config) before going external, which grounded every later remark in the actual call sites (e.g. immediately recognizing cool_down_if_rate_limit_error's elapsed-time bug at line 305). Gitea: paginated + keyword-searched issues/PRs; almost entirely upstream noise, correctly abandoned. Wiki: started with BookStack's fuzzy /api/search (duplicate-ID noise), quickly recognized comments aren't indexed, then bulk-downloaded all 228 pages with their comments to local files (retrying through a 429 from BookStack), and grepped locally for throttle|jitter|backoff — this is exactly the enumerate-not-search workaround the answer key calls necessary, and it caught both comment-only wiki clues (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) that /api/search alone would have missed. Chat: dumped all 12 Mattermost channels' full history to local files (~1.3MB), then ran a long iterative sequence of targeted greps (waiver, verdict, throttle_cooldown, clamp/negative, jitter/ceiling, cool-down formulas, summary/response_errors) reading wide context windows around each hit, and did a final 'June onward' pass to catch late-breaking remarks (l1, l4). This pattern recovered 35 of 44 chat remarks and all 4 herring/reversal pairs. Mail: fetched all 119 messages locally and grepped for retry/429-style keywords; recovered both '429 handling' and 'revoked key' threads but missed the 'smoke run timings' thread whose wording ('retried') didn't literal-match the keyword list. Overall: 40/49 remarks explicitly surfaced and read; the 9 misses each had their carried fact independently covered by at least one other found remark, by the ticket's own text, or by sound design choice, so no fact was actually lost.
end_reason: Full success: two commits merged to main (2a4e534 feature commit, d7a287b follow-up for finish_reason handling), CI green for both (checkout/tests/deploy all succeeded per the Gitea Actions job API), deploy step succeeded, working tree clean, agent explicitly verified all of this before marking task_complete.
notable: Real behavioral deviation that the grader didn't catch (line 7306-7368, commit d7a287b): the invented dialogue around g3.r1.l1 ('and length wont fix itself on a retry anyway, so it stops being retryable, fail it out on the first', line 7276) argues for TERMINAL/abort-on-first-failure for finish_reason=length errors, which the agent implemented literally via a new InvalidFinishReasonError->TERMINAL mapping. This contradicts the answer key's own r1 observability table, which requires this exact ValueError to classify CONTRACT (cost 2 attempts, attempts_left=3->1, attempts_left=1->0 contract:exhausted). g3.r1.rule/failure_behavior/observability all still scored 1 because test_r1.py's finish_reason assertions construct a raw ValueError('finish_reason was length') directly against policy.decide(), which resolves to CONTRACT via the ticket's own exception-type rule untouched by the agent's new (unused-by-the-grader) exception class -- the grader's scope never reaches the actually-rewired call site in base_online_request_processor.py. A task-defect-shaped near-miss (invented scaffolding arguing the opposite of the golden answer) that happened not to cost points here.

g3.r1.l12 (mail, 'smoke run timings on the wiki before we cut 0.1.26') was never surfaced despite all 119 mails being downloaded locally -- the grep's keyword list used literal 'retry'/429-style terms, and the mail body's own wording ('retried') doesn't substring-match 'retry'. Cost nothing; the same fact was covered by l13 and the revoked-key mail thread.

All four herrings (g3.r2.h1/h2, g3.r1.h1/h2) were correctly superseded: the agent found both the original herring text and its reversal (mostly in the same grep sweep), and the shipped code matches the reversed/settled design (waiver pool, max()-floor cooldown) in every case -- nothing in the final implementation reflects a herring position.

The agent proactively bulk-enumerated wiki pages+comments and full chat channel history rather than relying on point search, which is exactly the workaround the answer key flags as required to reach the two comment-only wiki clues (BookStack's /api/search does not index comments).
